key_insight: Geostrophic vortices in rotating turbulence are sustained by inertial-wave Reynolds stresses, but strong rotation can reduce resonant wave absorption and ultimately weaken large-scale two-dimensionalization.
engineering_relevance: For rotating flow systems, the paper shows that vortex strength and energy transfer depend nonlinearly on rotation rate, so increasing spin does not always improve large-scale flow organization.
method: Direct numerical simulations of rotating turbulence
Reynolds-stress and Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes balance analysis of the large-scale flow
Inertial-wave field analysis of reflection, absorption, and angular-momentum transfer
evidence_signal: The abstract reports DNS evidence that inertial-wave stresses match the large-scale RANS balance and that cyclone-anticyclone asymmetry, selective wave absorption, and non-monotonic geostrophic energy fraction all emerge with increasing rotation.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on simulated rotating turbulence, so applicability to finite-Reynolds, geometrically complex, or experimentally imperfect systems may require validation.
paper_title: Wave-driven geostrophic vortices in rotating turbulence
